name: Performing Arts
title: Performing Arts — Dance, Music and Theatre
intro: The performing arts roadmap: early training, degrees and institutes, auditions, performance and careers.

phases.title: Early training and guru-shishya practice
phases.summary: Regular training with a teacher matters most.
points: Start formal training in dance, vocal or instrumental music, or theatre under a qualified guru or institution.
Take graded exams offered by recognised music and dance bodies where available.
Perform in school and local events to build stage confidence.
Study theory, history and basic fitness or voice care.

phases.title: Degree and institute options
phases.summary: BA or Bachelor of Performing Arts, diplomas, or specialised institutes.
points: Universities such as BHU, Delhi University (via CUET-UG and auditions), Banaras, Kathak Kendra and others offer performing arts degrees.
National School of Drama (NSD) offers a three-year diploma in dramatic arts, with admission through a written test, workshop and audition.
Film and TV institutes (FTII, SRFTI) offer acting and related programmes via their entrance tests.
Choose a school based on faculty, performance exposure and alumni.

phases.title: Course structure
points: Learn technique in your chosen form: Kathak, Bharatanatyam, Hindustani/Carnatic music, Western music or theatre.
Study Natyashastra, music theory, history, aesthetics and stage craft.
Take practical performances and examinations each year.
Participate in productions and festivals.

phases.title: Performance, internships and exposure
phases.summary: Build a stage and recording record.
points: Perform at college fests, cultural festivals and in repertory productions.
Record audio or video portfolios of your work.
Intern with theatre groups, music studios or dance companies.
Apply for scholarships such as those from CCRT and the Ministry of Culture.

phases.title: Careers and higher study
points: Roles: stage performer, music or dance teacher, choreographer, composer, sound artist and arts administrator.
Higher study: MA/M.PA, PhD, and UGC NET for teaching in universities.
Government: All India Radio, Doordarshan, cultural centres and school teaching (with B.Ed).
Freelance and online teaching channels are growing.
